status: Scoped acknowledged account removal qualified locally; broader production readiness remains active.
behavior: Native primary, linked Ethereum, legacy/archive ECDSA and TON records are read from latest storage, copied exactly into a unique recovery entry, then removed in one grouped storage call. The archive and removal retain one store queue slot and share the vault queue with import/password/TON repair. Chrome uses separate acknowledged set/remove calls: a failed remove can retain an extra recovery copy, never an unarchived deletion.

Private keys/subjects remain live until removal acknowledgement; failure propagates without poisoning later retry. Publication locks and removes local pairs and publishes detached TON state without mutating previous observable snapshots. Missing durable primary records fail closed. Mobile removal validates the latest public identity and publishes removal only after acknowledgement.

Before a selected wallet is removed, State durably clears selection and Sora/context references. A failed selection clear aborts removal. Removal identities and epochs reject queued or new selections of that wallet, including SS58/EVM aliases. A newer explicit choice is not replaced by deletion fallback. Direct service callers also clear removed selection.

Message and incoming-session handlers await removal before cleanup/success. Explicit removal revokes permissions and retires sessions first. Captured primary pair, linked EVM/Solana/Iroha fields and mobile topic are revalidated before selection clear and inside the queued snapshot; changed identity/link causes a failed removal for explicit retry. Standalone primary and linked EVM grants clear case-insensitively.

Incoming mobile session-delete compares saved SS58 aliases by decoded identity so State context clearing and fallback apply. It validates the captured topic before clearing selection, and both deletion handlers guard the clear before/after storage acknowledgement. An obsolete event queued behind the vault cannot clear a wallet rebound to a newer topic.

IndexedDB reads, archives and deletes within one readwrite transaction and publishes after its commit. Three controlled adapter tests cover all reads, commit-only publication, abort and validation failure; this is not actual browser IndexedDB or cross-tab qualification.

reviewConclusions: Native and TON removal share the vault queue with imports/password operations; latest durable records are archived before acknowledged removal and in-memory deletion.

Chrome archive set and grouped removal are separate acknowledged operations; a failed removal may leave an extra recovery copy while live keys remain. IndexedDB uses one modeled read/write transaction.
Selection removal revisions reject pending and new choices of removed identities; successful selection clearing routes through State for context cleanup, with later user choices preserved.

Actual installed-keyring tests cover acknowledged failures, retry, grouped linked-key copies, selection and metadata races. Compiled Chrome harness checks four key curves, TON and public mobile records, exact recovery copies and two worker restarts, without relay negotiation.

limits: Chrome recovery-write/remove is not one crash-atomic transaction. Termination after recovery write can leave a still-active wallet plus hidden recovery copy. Failed removal may leave duplicate recovery copies and prior site/session revocation or cleared selection; private records and live accounts remain. Failed physical storage is not claimed durable.

Existing recovery restore remains a separate gate: writeBackDeletedWallet presence reads and later replaceAndWait are outside the vault transaction, can race import/password rotation, and publish through ui-keyring loadAccount. Normal restart/restore/export passed, not concurrent restore durability.
Whole-wallet reset, password partial-failure recovery, external storage mutation, real browser IndexedDB/cross-tab coordination, abrupt disk/power failures and every service cache remain unqualified.

Public unfunded fixtures only. No real relay/phone negotiation, physical assistive technology, new UI/locale acceptance, historical final-artifact upgrades, private-chain final sends or production publication is claimed.

The private-key archive remains on-device by the approved deletion/recovery invariant; account removal is not key erasure. Shared-linked-key ownership semantics, undeclared link discovery and broader wallet cleanup remain separate policy/coverage gates.
